chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Lays Al-Murady, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the day of Fitr or the day of Adha: 'If only you would pray in your mosque?' So he said: 'I love to come out to the horizons of the sky.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prefer to pray Eid prayers in open areas rather than in the mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the Prophetic preference for performing Eid prayers in open fields (*musalla*) rather than enclosed mosques, emphasizing the communal visibility and joy of the occasion. The phrase 'horizons of the sky' (*afāq al-samā’*) reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of the ritual's public nature, distinguishing it from the more intimate daily prayers. This practice underscores the social dimension of Eid, where the Ummah gathers visibly to celebrate divine blessings.
